title: Interest Since the Last Statement in a PracticePay Patient Financing Payoff
content:
**Rule.** The interest-since-closing rule of a PracticePay Patient Financing payoff follows the plan's promotion and its latest payment: on a deferred-interest plan whose promotional period end date is today or later and which carries no deferred-interest billing entry, a payoff today meets the promotional payoff test and no interest is added, neither since the closing nor for any good-through day; otherwise, when the plan's latest payment entry, the one recorded first where two share the latest date, is dated after the latest statement closing and has not come back as a returned payment, interest runs from the closing to that payment's date on the interest-bearing balance plus the amounts of every payment entry dated that day and from that payment's date through today on the interest-bearing balance; in every other case interest runs as one span on the interest-bearing balance.

Spans are counted from the day after their start date through their end date, and interest is simple interest at the plan's daily interest rate.

## The three cases

| Situation on the plan's records | Interest since the closing |
|---|---|
| deferred-interest plan, promotional period ending today or later, no deferred-interest billing entry | none; and no interest for any good-through day either |
| otherwise: latest payment entry dated after the latest statement closing and not come back | two spans: closing to the payment date on the interest-bearing balance plus every payment entry dated that day; then payment date through today on the interest-bearing balance |
| every other case | one span on the interest-bearing balance |

"Not come back" means no returned-payment entry names that payment. Where two payment entries share the latest date, the one recorded first is the latest payment entry, and the amounts of all payment entries dated that day are added back for the first span.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

Interest-bearing balance 1000.00 USD, daily rate 0.0005, latest statement closing on day 0, today day 10.

- A payment of 200.00 USD dated day 4 that has not come back: 1200.00 times 0.0005 times 4 days, that is 2.40, plus 1000.00 times 0.0005 times 6 days, that is 3.00; interest since the closing 5.40.
- The same payment came back: one span, 1000.00 times 0.0005 times 10 days, that is 5.00.
- A deferred-interest plan still inside its promotion with no billing entry: 0.00, and the good-through days carry 0.00 interest.
